policy_title: Leave the European Convention on Human Rights and reform the Human Rights Act
stated: Reform UK will leave the European Convention on Human Rights and commence reform of the Human Rights Act to prioritise the rights of law-abiding people.

source.quote: Leave the European Convention on Human Rights Commence reform of the Human Rights Act so that it puts the rights of law-abiding people first.

bearing_set.reason: Leaving the ECHR and reforming the HRA directly dismantles the UK's foundational legal framework for civil liberties, due process, equal treatment, privacy, and democratic rights — a non-negligible verdict on the rights-and-freedoms fundamental is unavoidable.

The stated rationale — 'prioritise the rights of law-abiding people' — directly targets criminal justice constraints (e.g. deportation of foreign nationals, sentencing limits) imposed by ECHR/HRA, making the effect on policing, courts, and national security non-negligible rather than incidental.

Articles 5 (liberty), 8 (privacy/family life), and 10 (free expression) of the ECHR are the international legal backstop against state surveillance, arbitrary detention, and speech restriction; leaving removes that constraint, plausibly widening the state's coercive latitude over individuals.

membership_note: Three genuine bearings: the safety/security benefit side (O5), the equal-treatment and due-process harm side (O9), and the personal-liberty harm side (O10). All three have named mechanisms and specific indicators. No fiscal, housing, or health bearing is plausible at non-negligible magnitude.
